refuted.item: "Дозапрос / same-context repair is unavailable with native primitives — a Claude Code subagent is one-shot and there is no continuation without Agent Teams." (architecture/opus drop-list; execution/opus conflict; quality/opus drop-list; economy/opus conflict; execution/sonnet conflict)
refuted.reason: Factually wrong on this build. SendMessage is live in Claude Code 2.1.232 and its own contract states verbatim: "names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript)", plus `to: "main"` for background subagents. Resumption is a shipped primitive. The correct objection is narrower and different in kind: it applies to NAMED / `background: true` subagents and Agent-Teams teammates, not to a plain Task dispatch, and Agent Teams remains gated behind CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 — which I verified IS set in this machine's env, i.e. the maintainer has it and vulyk's public users do not. So this is a distribution/positioning blocker against vulyk's "no experimental flags required" promise, not a capability gap. Every lens that wrote "impossible" should have written "gated, and shipping it makes the framework depend on an experimental flag."

refuted.item: "'A wave is not a barrier' (launch the next story the moment its blockers clear, process returns as they land) is unimplementable with native fan-out — parallel Task calls resolve into one assistant turn." (architecture/opus)
refuted.reason: True of the Task tool, false as a general claim. `background: true` is a documented subagent frontmatter field; background agents report asynchronously (SendMessage to:"main"), and Monitor + TaskStop are first-class tools whose notifications arrive mid-turn. Continuous-frontier dispatch is mechanically possible today. The real reasons not to ship it are the same experimental gate plus the fact that eight asynchronous returns land in the one context that is never refreshed — cost and positioning, not impossibility.

refuted.item: "A rule can live in `.claude/rules/tests.md` and cost nothing per dispatch, because path-scoped rules load on touch." (economy/opus, used to refute autopilot's "a rule that lives only in a phase file does not exist for the executor")
refuted.reason: `.claude/rules/` is not a Claude Code primitive. Verified in the repo: `.claude/rules/README.md` asserts "Rules here load only when work touches their declared paths" and `example-api.md` carries a `paths:` frontmatter — but nothing loads them. `.claude/settings.json` wires exactly six hooks (session-start-brief, handoff on 4 events, session-end-learnings, skill-usage-counter, context-guard); none injects rules. The only real delivery mechanism is `vulyk-build.md` step 3, where the QUEEN hands the worker "the relevant `.claude/rules/` paths" — paths, not contents, requiring a Read the worker may not spend on a file the Queen may have picked wrong. Autopilot's position is correct here, and vulyk's own doc claim needs correcting before anything is built on it.

refuted.item: "CLAUDE.md and path-scoped rules reach every subagent for free, so vulyk needs no per-dispatch prompt inlining." (economy/opus, stated as the vulyk side of the conflict)
refuted.reason: Not safe to assume, and the Aug-2026 subagent docs undercut it: `memory` is a listed subagent frontmatter field. A configurable memory-loading knob means memory loading is not a uniform freebie. Combined with the `.claude/rules/` refutation, the merged framework must treat "what reaches an executor" as a measured fact per field, not a design premise. Notably nobody in the panel proposed using `memory:`, `hooks:` or `skills:` in agent frontmatter — those are the actual native answers to this problem and they are unexplored.

refuted.item: "Adopt marker-wrapped CLAUDE.md as the canonical memory entry point, filled from the layer files — CLAUDE.md becomes a projection of the layers." (memory/haiku)
refuted.reason: Inverts the token economy it claims to serve. CLAUDE.md is loaded into every context in the session; making it a generated projection of a 7-layer plane means the always-loaded file grows with the repo — exactly what the ≤60-line pointer index (`memory/memory.md`) exists to prevent. The same lens also proposes dropping the SessionEnd hook for "Phase-gated moments", i.e. replacing a deterministic harness event with the model remembering to write memory. Hooks fire; prose instructions get skipped under load. The only transferable part is the marker discipline, which vulyk already ships (VULYK:COMMANDS:START/END) and should merely generalize to `## Project profile`.

refuted.item: "Move story status out of frontmatter into a central state.js; keep story files immutable." (execution/haiku; made v0.5.0-mandatory by architecture/haiku)
refuted.reason: Breaks the two consumers that exist. `/vulyk-status` and `context-guard.sh` read story frontmatter cheaply; state.js is `window.STATE = {…}` — a JS assignment, not JSON — so no shell tool in the repo can parse it without stripping the assignment. It also makes a generated, non-diffable artifact the source of truth in a framework whose stated memory-plane design is git-diffable prose. If a machine-readable run record is wanted it should be state.json DERIVED from frontmatter, never a replacement for it. Note the panel contradicts itself here: architecture/haiku calls it mandatory for v0.5.0 while ux/opus and both release lenses correctly rank the dashboard the lowest-measured-value item in either repo.

refuted.item: "Create `.autopilot/` directory structure parallel to docs/specs/" (execution/haiku, memory/haiku) and "keep both — .autopilot/ for working files, docs/specs/ for archive" (architecture/haiku)
refuted.reason: A second storage plane contradicts the README's explicit promise that the memory plane lives in git under `docs/`, and the haiku lenses contradict each other inside the same panel (memory/haiku simultaneously rules "Git is truth, .autopilot/ is staging"). There is no feasibility argument for it: `docs/specs/<slug>/` already exists, install.sh already creates it, and `copy_tree` already walks it. Drop the directory entirely.

refuted.item: "The Aug-2026 docs listing `effort` as a subagent frontmatter field settles the conflict — per-caste effort routing is now available."
refuted.reason: The docs do not refute the measurement. A behavioral measurement on Claude Code 2.1.220 (July 2026) recorded `effort:` in `.claude/agents/*.md` as silently inert and inverted (low → 8,819 output tokens, max → 4,541), and identified that the zod "Definition for a custom subagent" schema carrying `effort` belongs to the `--agents <json>` / SDK path, not markdown frontmatter — `effort: banana` raises no error while `model:` from the same frontmatter applies. Corroborating evidence this session: `CLAUDE_EFFORT=high` is exported as a process env var while the repo's settings.json says `effortLevel: medium`, consistent with effort being a launch/session parameter. Build is now 2.1.232 so a re-measure is warranted, but until it runs, no design may depend on per-caste effort and vulyk's CLAUDE.md text stands. A doc listing a field is not evidence that the markdown code path reads it — that is precisely the trap this was caught in the first time.

refuted.item: "The dashboard is one static HTML file with zero deps, fully native and subscription-safe" (quality/opus, ux/opus, architecture/haiku) — and, inversely, "file:// polling just works."
refuted.reason: Both framings are wrong in opposite directions and autopilot has already measured the truth. `phases/0-instruments.md` records (2026-08-13) that an in-app pane does not open file:// as a page — it inlines the HTML into `data:text/html`, after which `location.origin` is "null", `<script src="state.js">` resolves to nothing, fetch is CORS-cut, and BOTH `location.reload()` and `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` are silenced. The only mechanism that works everywhere is appending a fresh `<script src="state.js?t=…">`. Consequence: any lens proposing "poll state.js every 10s" without importing that specific mechanism ships a permanently blank dashboard, and in-pane display genuinely requires a `python3 -m http.server` process — real added surface, not zero deps.

refuted.item: "Delete the Workflows API roadmap line" as a complete fix for that overclaim (release/opus)
refuted.reason: Right diagnosis, incomplete fix — and the lens missed the bigger artifact. vulyk already SHIPS `.claude/workflows/README.md` and `.claude/workflows/feature.workflow.example.js` into every install via copy_tree, promising a harness feature that the Aug-2026 check finds no product behind (there is the Claude Agent SDK and Claude Code dynamic workflows; no standalone Workflows API). Deleting one README line while the installed tree still carries a `.workflow.js` example leaves the overclaim in the product, which is worse than leaving the line.

refuted.item: "Persistent per-run reviewers must fall back to `review-notes.md` on disk because stock Claude Code cannot continue a finished subagent." (economy/opus, quality/opus)
refuted.reason: The disk fallback is the right design; the stated justification is false (see the SendMessage refutation). State it as a deliberate trade — cross-story panorama via a committed notes file, chosen over an experimental-flag dependency — not as a harness limitation. This matters because the false version will be re-derived and re-litigated by the first contributor who reads the SendMessage docs.

refuted.item: "A PreToolUse hook denying Edit/Write/Bash to the main session is the missing technical enforcement of Rule 5" (architecture/sonnet) / "a secrets-blocking hook would break vulyk's fail-open hook contract" (safety/sonnet)
refuted.reason: Both wrong, in different places. Blocking does not break fail-open: a PreToolUse hook returns a permission decision (`deny`) — a designed outcome, not a crash — so no contract exception is needed. The actual blocker is scoping: PreToolUse fires for subagent tool calls too, and the hook payload gives no reliable "this is the main session, not a worker" discriminator (SubagentStart/SubagentStop are lifecycle events, not a per-call flag), so a naive deny-rule would also gag worker-code. Rule 5 stays prose-enforced until someone proves a discriminator exists — and that verification, not the hook, is the shippable task.

refuted.item: "Autopilot's persistent reviewers keep cross-ticket memory by being 'refreshed at wave boundaries'" imported as a v0.5.0 must (quality/haiku, economy/haiku)
refuted.reason: Compounds two unverified things into a mandatory release item: reviewer continuation (gated, per above) and per-story Opus review (the exact ceremony tax the 2026 landscape data punishes BMAD for). quality/haiku's own text admits it "requires Claude Code subagent-continuation support" and then schedules it anyway. A framework cannot ship a v0.5.0 must whose mechanism is behind an experimental env flag its README promises not to require.

weak: Manifest / R##-A##-D##-G## ledger as a v0.5.0 'must' at every tier (architecture/haiku, quality/haiku, memory/haiku). The idea is sound and the row-ID taxonomy is cheap markdown, but three lenses rank it must-adopt without noticing it has zero anchor: vulyk never persists the human's verbatim request anywhere, so a manifest built at plan time is a paraphrase indexing a paraphrase. Downgrade to: brief.md first (one line of change), manifest second, gates third.

G2/G4 blind-acceptance gates as headline v0.5.0 items. Mechanically feasible (a subagent with Read/Bash and a deliberately starved context is exactly what subagents are for), but conditional in practice: vulyk's own `## Commands` table honestly ships 'Full suite / build: none exists', and library/migration/refactor work — most of vulyk's Tier 2-3 traffic — has no main scenario to walk. An unconditional G4 manufactures theatre on precisely the work vulyk is best at. Ship it gated on 'a run command exists', failing loudly-absent rather than silently-passing.

Three-axis review (Manifest/Spec/Craft) as a replacement for BLOCK/PASS (quality/haiku, architecture/haiku). Real information gain, but the cost is misstated: it is either a six-point protocol on one Opus reviewer (the ceremony load both frameworks warn against) or two dispatches per gate with no model diversity — strictly worse than vulyk's existing Tier-4 different-model second reviewer, which is grounded in actual CodeRabbit precision/recall data. Axis LABELS inside one reviewer's report cost nothing; axis SEPARATION should stay Tier 4 only.

The dashboard/state.js instrument generally. Genuinely the best demo asset in either repo, and the poll mechanism is measured and correct — but it is a second source of truth alongside story frontmatter, needs an http server for in-pane display, and the 79KB template multiplied per spec is larger than the artifacts it displays. Every lens that ranked it must (architecture/haiku, ux/haiku) over-weighted a screenshot against the merge's actual thesis.

'One story = one commit' framed as a rollback-points nicety (execution/sonnet, execution/haiku). Under-rated, not over-rated — see musts. It is the fix for a confirmed live bug, and treating it as a UX improvement buries that.

The mode dial (full/semi/interview/manual) as a v0.5.0 UX item. Pure prompt text, so near-zero implementation cost — but `full` mode is a constitutional contradiction with Law 1, not a settings choice, and the panel is split three ways on whether it ships at all. Land the announce block and the tier readout first; the dial is worthless until the Law 1 question is answered in writing.

Payback/neighbour tests and the story-density merge pass. Correct and cheap, but presented by three lenses as a token-economy discovery when it is really a planning heuristic with a made-up constant (the 20-40k re-orientation figure is an estimate nobody in either repo measured). Ship the heuristic; do not ship the number as if it were measured — vulyk's whole credibility asset is not doing that.

`interfaces.md` as a standalone run-scoped file (five lenses want the file; architecture/opus and pipeline/opus want it as a plan.md section). The content is essential before any parallel wave; the separate file adds an eighth memory-plane artifact with its own writer discipline and lifecycle. The section form gets the same benefit with none of the plane cost.
top_musts: Close the confirmed secrets leak in `memory/learnings/`. Verified: `.gitignore` covers `memory/snapshots/`, `memory/map/.stale` and `.claude/handoff/` — but NOT `memory/learnings/`, and `session-end-learnings.sh` pipes `tail -c 200000` of the raw transcript through headless Haiku straight into that git-tracked directory under VULYK_AUTOLEARN=1, from where `librarian` folds it into a committed CONSOLIDATED.md. This is a live leak path today, independent of the merge, and it becomes structural the moment verbatim briefs land on disk. Fix = one .gitignore decision + `scripts/redact.sh` (autopilot's regex table, fail-open, exit 0) piped into the hook. Cheapest high-severity item in the whole panel.

Fix the scope-gate contamination by committing per story. Verified in `scripts/scope-check.sh`: the default range is `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus untracked files, and the script's own docstring justifies that with "VULYK's build loop does not commit per story." So story 03's scope check counts story 01's and 02's files as out-of-scope — the framework's ONLY objective metric is broken from the second story of every build onward. Per-story commits (gated on scope-check + green quiet verification) fix it for free and give real rollback points. Note the blast radius: it also changes what `/vulyk-review` reviews (commit range vs working tree) and the post-merge hook's staleness timing.

Get the full verification suite out of the Queen's session. Verified: `vulyk-build.md` step 6 says "run the project's full verification command once" — in the main session — while CLAUDE.md line 75 states that command output under 30,000 characters lands in the transcript verbatim and is resent every turn after. The framework violates its own most-quantified rule in its own build loop. Route it to a subagent whose context dies, or pipe the quiet variant through `tail -30`.

Bounded return contract on `worker-code` and `worker-test` (STATUS/FILES/TESTS/INTERFACES/CONCERNS/BLOCKERS, ≤25 lines, no code, no diffs). Highest value-per-line item that needs nothing else to land. Returns are decoded output at ~5x input price and then resident permanently in the one context never refreshed. Include NEEDS_CONTEXT as a distinct status from the existing 3-approach wall — they route to different people.

`wave:` + `blocked_by:` in story frontmatter plus a deterministic `## Files` overlap check before co-dispatch. This closes a real correctness hole, not a nicety: `vulyk-build.md` step 2 dispatches up to 4 concurrent workers with no mechanism computing independence, and two workers editing one file overwrite each other silently. vulyk already owns the raw material — the machine-readable `## Files` block scope-check.sh parses. A `scripts/wave-check.sh` in the same shape (report-only, exit 0) is ~40 lines.

Say explicitly that a wave launches in ONE message, one dispatch per story. This is the actual mechanism behind parallelism — multiple tool calls in a single assistant turn — and `vulyk-build.md` names a cap of 4 without ever naming it. Two calls in two messages run serially and the transcript looks identical to a correct run. One load-bearing sentence.

Persist the human's verbatim request to `docs/specs/<slug>/brief.md` at `/vulyk-plan` step 1. One line of change, and it is the anchor that every later gate (G2 coverage, G4 blind acceptance, manifest Basis column, the story-level `## From the ask` quotes) needs in order to be more than a paraphrase checking a paraphrase. Ship it in v0.5.0 even if none of those gates do.

Scope the Queen's-keyboard rule to a tier floor and write it down. Autopilot's Rule 5 as written contradicts vulyk's Tier 0 row ('do it directly, no ceremony') head-on; unscoped it is decorative and the model will read it either way it likes. The defensible line is "from the moment a story file exists" (equivalently Tier 2 up). Then close the two loopholes: `vulyk-review.md` step 4 currently forbids hand-patching only CRITICALS, which licenses hand-patching everything else, and `vulyk-build.md` step 4's 're-scope the story' is an unrecorded requirement-narrowing path.

Re-measure `effort:` in agent frontmatter on 2.1.232 before any design touches it, and fix the CLAUDE.md-vs-model-cascade.md Haiku/Sonnet contradiction the same afternoon. Both are blockers for assigning models to the new castes the merge adds (coverage checker, blind checker, memory writer), and both are one experiment each. Guessing either propagates the error into every new agent file.

Seed the boundaries/interfaces contract before wave 1 — as a `## Contracts` section of plan.md, not a new file. Parallel workers with only a story file and a map slice have nothing describing what their concurrent siblings are building, and `memory/map/` describes what EXISTS, i.e. the old code. This is the one thing standing between a 4-wide wave and story 06 reinventing story 03's helper, and it must not slip behind the pipeline driver.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Subagent lifecycle: can a completed subagent be resumed by message (дозапрос, persistent reviewers, launch-on-return)?
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Yes, natively — but only for named/background agents, and only behind CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1. Therefore: keep vulyk's fresh-worker fallback as the shipped default, adopt autopilot's TRANSFERABLE half unconditionally (a repair is stated as a checkable condition — 'this test green' — never 'поправь'; ceiling of 2 repairs before it becomes a failed story), and record in CLAUDE.md that the cheap path exists but is flag-gated, so nobody re-derives it. Do not ship an opt-in Teams profile even for Tier 4 in v0.5.0.
conflict_resolutions.why: SendMessage's own contract says a send by name 'resumes it from its transcript', so 'impossible' is refutable and will be refuted by the first contributor who reads the docs. But the flag is set on the maintainer's machine and not on users' — shipping against it silently breaks the README's native-primitives-only promise, which is vulyk's positioning moat. Writing down WHY the cheap path is unavailable is worth more than either shipping or omitting it.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Review timing: per-story inline review (autopilot) vs one adversarial gate at the end (vulyk). Eight lenses split, several ruling opposite ways.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Keep `/vulyk-review` as the single Opus merge gate. Inside the build loop, run only the deterministic pair per story — scope-check.sh plus the story's quiet `## Verification` command — and gate the commit on them. Escalate to anything resembling per-story model review at Tier 4 only, where vulyk already pays for a second reviewer.
conflict_resolutions.why: Per-story Opus review is the exact ceremony tax the 2026 landscape data records BMAD losing users over, and the amortisation that makes autopilot's version affordable (a reviewer kept alive across tickets) is flag-gated. Without that amortisation vulyk gets the cost with none of the mitigation. The cross-story finding autopilot buys is genuinely forfeited — but a single reviewer reading the whole diff at the gate recovers most of it for free, which per-story review structurally cannot.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Two tier scales: vulyk Tier 0-4 (blast radius, decided before work) vs autopilot T0-T3 (product shape / ticket count, decided at the cut).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: vulyk's Tier 0-4 is the only thing called a tier. Import autopilot's story-count budgets and the >16 ceiling as a column on the existing routing-matrix rows (T0→Tier 0-1, T1→Tier 2 at 2-4 stories, T2→Tier 3 at 4-8, T3→Tier 4 at 9-16, above 16 = split into two specs). Delete the T-labels from every file.
conflict_resolutions.why: Both scales would print on the same status line and appear in the same README, making 'what tier is this' ambiguous in every planning conversation — which is autopilot's own one-word-per-concept rule violated by importing autopilot. The counts are the useful half and they graft onto rows that already exist. No feasibility issue either way; this is pure comprehension cost, and it is paid in the most expensive context.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: File paths in the unit of work: autopilot forbids them in tickets ('they go stale faster than the ticket'); vulyk requires a machine-readable `## Files` block.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: vulyk wins outright. Keep `## Files` exactly as-is, and add autopilot's zone as a SEPARATE concept (directory-level ownership, used only for wave-collision serialization).
conflict_resolutions.why: `## Files` is the parsed input to `scope-check.sh` — the only zero-token, model-free, un-gameable metric in either framework, and the one deliberately built with a second number (`declared`) so the first cannot be gamed. Autopilot has no equivalent; its scope discipline is prose plus a reviewer's judgement. Autopilot's own zone rule proves path-level ownership has to be written down somewhere anyway. Zone and Files are different objects: zone prevents concurrent collision, Files bounds one worker.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Gate authority: autopilot's 'a failed gate is not a warning, the phase is redone' vs scope-check.sh's deliberate always-exit-0.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Write the split as policy, not inherit it as an accident: the deterministic layer measures and never blocks; the model layer (lead-review, and any imported G2/G4) judges and may BLOCK; the human overrides either, out loud. Any new deterministic gate (coverage-check, wave-check) ships with the same exit-0 contract as its sibling.
conflict_resolutions.why: scope-check.sh's own comment names the reason and it is correct: a deterministic check has deterministic false positives — an out-of-scope file is either a bad story or a wide worker and the script cannot tell which. Auto-blocking on it trains planners to declare half the repo, which is precisely what the `declared` counter exists to catch. Model-judged gates have no such structural false-positive mode and can afford to block.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Approval by default: vulyk's unconditional Tier 3-4 human gate vs autopilot's semi/full modes that never wait, plus Law 1 ('no silent assumptions') vs `full` mode which asks nothing.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Default stays gated. If `full` ships at all, it ships as the single explicitly-named, opt-in waiver of Law 1, conditional on every assumption it would have asked about being recorded verbatim and reprinted in the final report. Not in v0.5.0 — CLAUDE.md must say this in writing before any code path can take it.
conflict_resolutions.why: CLAUDE.md is loaded on every prompt including subagents; leaving it asserting Law 1 while a shipped mode violates it makes the constitution untrue on every full run, which is worse than not having the mode. Law 1's real content is 'no SILENT assumptions' — the recorded-and-reported version preserves it. This is a constitutional edit, not a settings flag, and it is the one merge item that genuinely cannot be decided implicitly by whoever implements it.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Memory sourced from the plan vs from the code: drone-docs.md is fed the story file and told to read its `## Implementation notes`; autopilot's 9-memory.md explicitly withholds spec and tickets from the memory writer.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Autopilot wins. Rewrite drone-docs' input contract: the diff and the changed files are primary; the story names WHICH files to look at and is labelled as a plan that may be wrong; if notes and diff disagree, the diff wins and the disagreement is reported, not silently reconciled. Add a verify-before-write checklist (every path named must exist, every quoted command must have been run, omit what you cannot verify).
conflict_resolutions.why: drone-docs.md line 17 already asserts the right principle — 'You record what IS, not what should be' — and then its own input contract undercuts it. A map slice describing what a story INTENDED is worse than no slice, because vulyk's memory protocol treats the hint as at least code-derived. This is a prompt edit inside an existing caste, costs nothing, and closes the gap between what the file says and what it does.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Session length: autopilot's 'one dialogue, starting fresh means losing the run' vs vulyk's 'session length is the top cost lever, /clear between tiers', compounded by per-phase effort wanting to change mid-run.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Break the run at the planning→build boundary with `/vulyk-handoff` + `/clear`, and set effort once per session on each side. Autopilot's premise is false under vulyk anyway — brief, manifest, plan, stories and interfaces are all on disk, so the orchestrator context is replaceable, not irreplaceable.
conflict_resolutions.why: Effort is a launch/session parameter (confirmed: CLAUDE_EFFORT is exported as a process env var; settings.json carries effortLevel), and changing it mid-session re-renders the prompt and drops the cached prefix at exactly the point where the prefix is most expensive. Splitting at the boundary pays one deliberate cache break that also serves session hygiene, instead of paying an accidental one plus carrying planning-grade effort through the whole build.

refuted.item: [architecture/opus, first_minor_slice] "install.sh needs the new template in its copy list."
refuted.reason: Factually wrong. E:/Projects/vulyk/install.sh runs `for tree in .claude memory bootstrap templates scripts docs/wiki docs/specs docs/adr; do copy_tree "$tree"`, and copy_tree does a `find "$rel" -type f` walk. Any new file under templates/, scripts/ or .claude/ is copied with zero installer changes. pipeline/opus got this right; architecture/opus did not. Nobody should spend a v0.5.0 line item on it.

refuted.item: [execution/haiku, memory/haiku] "state.js centralization — move story status out of story frontmatter into a central dashboard state file" (and its dependents: `.autopilot/<slug>/` as a second storage root).
refuted.reason: Breaks three live invariants at once. (a) E:/Projects/vulyk/CLAUDE.md:117 makes `every story's status: line` a compact-preservation item, and .claude/hooks/context-guard.sh plus /vulyk-status both read it — moving the truth to a JS file leaves three consumers reading a stale carcass. (b) The Queen becomes the sole writer of a per-transition JSON edit in the one context the design never refreshes — the exact cost the same lens invokes Rule 5 to avoid. (c) `.autopilot/` is a second, non-diffable storage plane next to docs/specs/, contradicting README's explicit everything-in-git promise. Status lives in story frontmatter; derive a view, never duplicate the truth.

refuted.item: [execution/haiku] "Drop free-form story appends (`## Implementation notes`, `## Findings`) — replaced by the return contract."
refuted.reason: The return contract and the on-disk record are different artifacts with different consumers. E:/Projects/vulyk/.claude/agents/drone-docs.md protocol step 1 is literally "Read the story's `## Implementation notes` and the diff summary" — deleting that section decapitates the memory plane's only per-story input. `## Findings` is the wall rule's output in worker-code.md and the Queen's decision input in vulyk-build.md step 4. Keep both: the ≤25-line block is the wire format, the sections are the record.

refuted.item: [memory/haiku] "Adopt marker-wrapped CLAUDE.md as canonical memory; CLAUDE.md becomes a projection of the layers, written by a Phase-8 subagent."
refuted.reason: CLAUDE.md is the constitution, loaded into every context including every subagent's. Making it machine-generated hands a subagent ungated write access to the file that governs all future sessions, contradicting CLAUDE.md:138 ("Nothing self-applies — every change is a reviewable changeset") and CLAUDE.md:132 ("keep this file lean"). The code-derived description belongs in memory/map/ plus a new memory/overview.md with a pointer from CLAUDE.md — which is where memory/opus and memory/sonnet both landed.

refuted.item: [memory/haiku] "Drop hooks except skill-counter and pre-compaction snapshot; kill session-end-learnings."
refuted.reason: E:/Projects/vulyk/.claude/settings.json wires handoff.sh on SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PreCompact. Deleting all but two hooks removes the entire context-budget meter and session-restore layer — in a merge whose single biggest new risk is a longer, multi-phase session. It also contradicts the same lens's own keep list ("Session handoff hook and multi-session support").

refuted.item: [architecture/haiku, quality/haiku, ux/haiku] "state.js + dashboard.html mandatory for v0.5.0."
refuted.reason: Mandating an ~80KB HTML instrument in the release whose job is to prove the merge is coherent inverts the priority order: highest surface, lowest measured value in either framework, duplicates /vulyk-status, and is the only proposal needing a rendering/serving story vulyk has never had. Optional artifact, later minor, gitignored per-spec copy — or not at all.

refuted.item: [execution/haiku] "Story density: adopt Autopilot's ~2000-token ticket budget, raise the story budget from ~1500."
refuted.reason: Presented as a resolved conflict with zero evidence on either side. E:/Projects/vulyk/templates/story.md states the budget IS the forcing mechanism ("a story that does not fit is an epic wearing a disguise"). Swapping one project's arbitrary constant for another's is not a merge decision. Refuse until a real run produces a story that legitimately does not fit — and note docs/specs/ currently holds only a .gitkeep, so no run has ever produced one.

refuted.item: [architecture/haiku, quality/haiku] "Persistent per-ticket reviewers kept alive across the build" as a v0.5.0 must.
refuted.reason: Not a native Claude Code primitive. A Task subagent returns and is gone; continuation needs Agent Teams, which is experimental and env-gated (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1) and breaks the README's native-primitives/no-experimental-flags promise. Autopilot's own phase file names the fresh-context fallback. quality/haiku's conflict list admits it "requires Claude Code subagent-continuation support" and then ships it as must-adopt anyway — that is the incoherence.

refuted.item: [quality/haiku] "Replace binary BLOCK/PASS with per-axis verdicts; remove 'test theater' from lead-review; split into two reviewer agents."
refuted.reason: Three problems. (1) Splitting one opus reviewer into two doubles the most expensive dispatch in the cascade, against CLAUDE.md:71 (top model for planning and final review only). (2) Autopilot's craft prompt has no security dimension; lead-review.md's protocol does (injection, authz on new endpoints, secrets, unsafe deserialization, path traversal). Swapping protocols loses it. (3) A merge gate with per-axis verdicts and no single call forces the human to aggregate — the opposite of what a gate is for. Label the report by axis inside the existing single reviewer; keep BLOCK/PASS.

refuted.item: [safety/*, architecture/*] Rule 5 ("the orchestrator never writes the project's code") imported unscoped.
refuted.reason: Unscoped it contradicts E:/Projects/vulyk/CLAUDE.md:48 (Tier 0: "Do it directly. No ceremony.") and CLAUDE.md:30-33 ("Do not delegate what you can finish in a handful of tool calls") inside the same file that would carry it. A constitution that contradicts itself on page one gives the model a licensed excuse in whichever direction it prefers. Only the scoped split survives — see resolutions.

refuted.item: [ux/haiku] "Russian one-word stage names on the dashboard and in /vulyk-status, as a MUST."
refuted.reason: vulyk is an English public MIT repo; every agent, command, template and doc is English. Importing autopilot's Russian stage vocabulary creates exactly the two-vocabularies problem the imported rule exists to prevent, and the same lens elsewhere says "keep English in code/CLAUDE.md" — incoherent within one submission. Keep the rule (one word per stage, same word everywhere), instantiate it in English.

refuted.item: [release/haiku] Storage: `.vulyk/specs/<slug>/manifest.md` in the first_minor_slice while the same lens's own conflict list recommends `docs/specs/<slug>/manifest.md`.
refuted.reason: Self-contradictory within a single submission, and the proposed new root would fork the memory plane. docs/specs/ already exists, is created and copied by install.sh, and is where plan.md and story files live.

weak: interfaces.md as a NEW run-scoped file. Six lenses call it a must; it is a fourth artifact handed to every worker (story + map slice + rules + interfaces), which widens the scoped-context law it is supposed to serve, and it duplicates half of memory/map/ with no writer discipline and no last-verified date. pipeline/opus is right: it should be a `## Contracts` section (owns / exposes / hides + named test seams) inside a plan.md template that does not exist yet — E:/Projects/vulyk/templates/ holds only adr.md, story.md, wiki-note.md. Same content, one fewer plane.

Blind acceptance (G4) as an unconditional gate. Needs two things vulyk lacks: a verbatim brief (/vulyk-plan takes `$ARGUMENTS` and the earliest artifact is already a paraphrase) and a runnable product. CLAUDE.md:101 ships "Full suite / build: none exists" deliberately, and v0.4.2 exists specifically to stop false greens. On a library change or a migration a blind checker cannot walk a scenario, and inventing one is the exact defect the last release was cut to fix. Conditional, with a loud cannot-be-run-here branch, or nothing.

The full manifest (25-50 rows, 7 statuses, 5 update moments). Defensible at Tier 3-4 only. E:/Projects/vulyk/docs/specs/ and docs/adr/ contain a single .gitkeep each and memory/stats/ has no scope.jsonl — the pipeline has never been run once on a real spec and scope-check.sh has never scored a real story. A row-lifecycle ledger on an unexercised pipeline is machinery ahead of evidence, which is the ceremony failure the landscape data pins on BMAD. Tier 3-4 full, Tier 2 short (ask quoted into a Basis column, no separate brief file), Tier 0-1 never.

The Queen's-hands / keyboard-scope rule as a headline must. It is prose-only enforcement in a session with full tool permissions — architecture/sonnet is right that neither framework has a technical gate. Worth writing down, but it is a norm, not a fix, and should not be sold as closing the hole. The part that genuinely bites is narrower and should carry the weight: never finish a returned worker's story by hand, at any tier.

`## Zone` as a new story field. Redundant. templates/story.md already carries a machine-readable `## Files` block with a working awk parser at scripts/scope-check.sh lines 38-44. A second, prose-level ownership vocabulary that scope-check.sh does not parse creates two scope truths. The needed change is one sentence in vulyk-build.md: do not co-dispatch stories whose `## Files` declarations intersect. `wave:`/`blocked_by:` frontmatter is worth adding; `## Zone` is not.

Three-axis review (Manifest/Spec/Craft) as a structural change. The routing question ("could the worker have known?") is the transferable part and costs one line in lead-review.md. Splitting the dispatch is what costs money and gains nothing vulyk does not already get from one reviewer reading the whole diff at once.

The ≤25-line / ≤12-finding return cap applied to reviewers. Collides head-on with lead-review.md's explicit rule to report everything at every severity and not self-filter ("a reviewer told to report only what matters reliably finds less"). Cap workers; do not cap the gate. Take the reviewer's saving from format instead — one sentence per finding, stated as a condition, no code excerpts.

Modes (full/semi/interview/manual) plus the depth dial as v0.5.0 items. Four modes times three depths is a 12-cell cross-product that must appear in every command file, the README and the status line, to buy an escape hatch from a gate the framework itself calls "separate decisions by design". Three modes at most if any, and `full` not at all until Law 1 is explicitly amended.
top_musts: Fix the scope-gate contamination bug before adding anything on top of it. E:/Projects/vulyk/scripts/scope-check.sh defaults to `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus untracked files, and its own header states the build loop does not commit per story. So on any multi-story build, story 03's check counts story 01's and 02's files as out-of-scope — the framework's ONLY objective metric is wrong by construction for every story after the first, and /vulyk-review step 1 feeds those numbers into the review packet and into memory/stats/scope.jsonl. Fix by committing per story (updating the script docstring at lines 12-14) or by passing an explicit per-story range. A live defect, not a merge item — and every 'scope-check feeds the new gate' proposal in this panel is built on it.

Give install.sh a version stamp and an `--upgrade` path — this is the coherence blocker for the whole v0.5.0 plan. install.sh copies file-by-file and skips anything that already exists; there is no VERSION file anywhere in the repo. Every high-priority recommendation in this panel is an edit to an existing file (CLAUDE.md, .claude/agents/worker-code.md, .claude/commands/vulyk-build.md, templates/story.md). None of them can ever reach a project that already installed vulyk. Shipping five more minors of edits into a distribution model that cannot deliver edits is the largest incoherence in the merge.

Settle the drone model contradiction before assigning a model to any new caste. CLAUDE.md:71 says "recon, docs, and memory upkeep on Haiku"; .claude/agents/drone-scout.md, drone-docs.md and librarian.md all say `model: sonnet`; docs/architecture.md:16 and :21, docs/command-reference.md:6, docs/getting-started.md:26 and .claude/commands/vulyk-map.md:2 all still say Haiku. docs/model-cascade.md:48-55 already names the experiment that settles it. The merge adds three or four more cheap castes (coverage checker, blind checker, memory writer) that need this answer; propagating the drift into new files makes the framework's headline claim unauditable.

Re-measure `effort:` in agent frontmatter, then restate with a date and client version or retract. docs/model-cascade.md:81 records low → 8,819 output tokens, max → 4,541 ("inverted, i.e. no control at all"), and CLAUDE.md:54-57 and README:100 state it as law. Current official subagent docs list `effort` as a supported frontmatter field. One of the two is wrong, and the honesty section is this project's single credibility asset. Same prompt, two agent files differing only in `effort:`, compare output tokens.

Close the memory/learnings leak. .gitignore covers memory/snapshots/, memory/map/.stale and .claude/handoff/ but NOT memory/learnings/, and .claude/hooks/session-end-learnings.sh under VULYK_AUTOLEARN=1 pipes `tail -c 200000` of the raw transcript to headless Haiku and writes the result there, from which librarian folds it into a committed CONSOLIDATED.md. That is a git-tracked path from pasted user text today, before any merge, and it becomes an outright contradiction the moment verbatim brief capture lands. Add scripts/redact.sh as a stdin→stdout transform (same fail-open contract as the hooks: set -u, always exit 0) wired into session-end-learnings.sh and handoff.py's prompt extractor. A transform, not a blocking hook — the fail-open hook contract stays intact.

Make parallelism real and safe with two sentences in .claude/commands/vulyk-build.md, no new fields. Step 3: a wave goes out in ONE message, one Task call per story — two calls in two messages run serially and the transcript looks identical to a correct run. Step 2: never co-dispatch two stories whose `## Files` declarations intersect; reuse scope-check.sh's existing awk parser for the check. Today step 2 says "cap: 4 concurrent workers" with no mechanism that produces concurrency and nothing preventing two workers from overwriting the same file silently. Add `wave:` and `blocked_by:` to templates/story.md so the order is computed once at plan time rather than re-derived at dispatch.

Bound what comes back. Add a fixed `## Return` block to .claude/agents/worker-code.md and worker-test.md: STATUS (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT) / FILES (paths only) / TESTS (command → result) / INTERFACES / CONCERNS / BLOCKERS, ≤25 lines, no code, no diffs. Keep `## Implementation notes` and `## Findings` on disk unchanged — drone-docs.md reads the former, the wall rule writes the latter. Cheapest lever available: a return is decoded output at ~5x input price that then sits permanently in the one context never refreshed.

Fix vulyk-build.md step 6, which violates CLAUDE.md:75 inside the framework's own files. It tells the Queen to "run the project's full verification command once" in the main session; CLAUDE.md:75 says command output under 30,000 characters lands in the transcript verbatim and is resent every turn afterwards. Route it through a subagent, or pipe the quiet variant through `tail -30`. Same treatment for scope-check.sh output in vulyk-review.md step 1.

Add a repair ceiling and a descope record to vulyk-build.md step 4. Today: "decide: re-scope the story, send a fresh worker with the findings attached, or escalate" — unbounded retries and a unilateral, unrecorded scope change. Replace with: every repair stated as a checkable condition (never "improve it"), max two rounds, then the story is blocked and the human is told; and any re-scope appends a `## Descoped` block to the story naming what left and why, surfaced at /vulyk-review. Dropping an acceptance criterion outright stays the human's call. This is the only part of autopilot's requirement-protection rule vulyk can actually enforce with what it has today.

Persist the human's verbatim request. One line in .claude/commands/vulyk-plan.md step 1: write `$ARGUMENTS` (redacted) to docs/specs/<slug>/brief.md, never edited, additions appended and dated. Costs a file write and unblocks every later independence-based gate (coverage, blind acceptance), which are otherwise impossible — vulyk's earliest artifact today is already a paraphrase, so a "blind" checker could only be blind to stories while still reading the plan. Do NOT ship the manifest, the gates or the modes in the same release: land the anchor, then let a real run show whether the gates earn their cost.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Review timing: per-story inline review (autopilot) vs one end-of-build opus gate (/vulyk-review).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: The end gate stays the only model review. Per-story becomes the deterministic pair only: scope-check.sh plus the story's own quiet `## Verification` command. No lead-review dispatch inside the build loop, at any tier.
conflict_resolutions.why: Per-story opus contradicts CLAUDE.md:71 (top model for planning and final review only), and the amortisation autopilot uses to make it affordable — a reviewer resumed across tickets — is not a native primitive. Taking the cost without the mitigation is the worst of both. A single reviewer reading the whole diff also gets the cross-story contradiction finding for free, which was the main thing per-ticket review was buying.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Two complexity scales: vulyk Tier 0-4 (blast radius, before work) vs autopilot T0-T3 (ticket count, at the cut).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: vulyk's Tier 0-4 is the only thing called a tier. Import the story-count budgets as a new column on the existing matrix in CLAUDE.md (Tier 0 none, 1 = 1-3, 2 = 2-4, 3 = 4-8, 4 = 9-16, >16 = split into two specs). The T0-T3 labels appear nowhere in the merged framework.
conflict_resolutions.why: The matrix at CLAUDE.md:46-52 is referenced by every command, every agent and the README, and it routes models — the expensive decision. Autopilot's scale routes nothing; only its numbers are useful, and they graft onto existing rows without inventing a second vocabulary.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Rule 5 (orchestrator never writes code) vs Tier 0 ("Do it directly. No ceremony.") and delegation restraint.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Two rules, not one. (a) The keyboard scope binds from the moment a story file exists for the work in hand — i.e. inside /vulyk-build, at any tier. (b) At every tier including 0 and 1: never finish a returned or stalled worker's story by hand; it goes back down as a condition or to a fresh worker. Tier 0-1 direct work before any dispatch stands untouched.
conflict_resolutions.why: Unscoped, the rule contradicts CLAUDE.md:48 and CLAUDE.md:30-33 in the same file that carries it, which makes it decorative. Split this way, the half that actually costs money — a diff read at story 02 still resident at story 08 — is the half that binds, and the half vulyk deliberately kept (don't dispatch a subagent for a two-call edit) survives intact.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Approval gate: unconditional stop at /vulyk-plan vs autopilot's semi/full modes that never gate.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: The gate stays unconditional in v0.5.0. `full` mode is not shipped. If it ever is, it must be a named, documented waiver of Law 1 with every would-have-been-a-question assumption recorded verbatim and reprinted at the end.
conflict_resolutions.why: CLAUDE.md:15 (Law 1) is loaded into every context including every subagent's. A mode that silently makes it untrue leaves the constitution lying in every prompt of that run. There is no way to hold both without amending Law 1 out loud, and no reason to do that in the release whose job is proving the merge is coherent.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: File paths in the unit of work: autopilot forbids them in tickets; vulyk requires the machine-readable `## Files` block.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: `## Files` wins outright and no zone field is added. `wave:`/`blocked_by:` go into frontmatter; collision detection reuses the `## Files` parser.
conflict_resolutions.why: `## Files` is the sole input to scripts/scope-check.sh — the only zero-token, model-free, un-gameable measurement in either framework and the operational form of Law 3. Autopilot's own zone rule concedes path-level ownership has to be written down somewhere; vulyk already writes it in a form a script can read.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Gate authority: autopilot's "a failed gate sends the phase back" vs scope-check.sh's deliberate `exit 0` ("this reports, it does not block").
conflict_resolutions.resolution: State it once as policy: deterministic scripts measure and never block; model verdicts (lead-review BLOCK) can block; the human overrides either, out loud and on the record.
conflict_resolutions.why: A deterministic check has deterministic false positives — scope-check.sh's own comment says an out-of-scope file is either a bad story or a wide worker and the script cannot tell which. Auto-blocking on it trains planners to declare half the repo, which is exactly what the `declared` counter exists to catch. Left unstated, the merged constitution carries both principles and no reader can tell which applies to which artifact.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Storage plane: `.autopilot/<slug>/` (run-scoped, dies with the run) vs `docs/specs/<slug>/` (git-tracked, permanent).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: docs/specs/<slug>/ only. brief.md, plan.md, story files and any plan deltas land there. Nothing gets a new root; if a machine-readable run view is ever wanted it goes under memory/stats/ or is gitignored.
conflict_resolutions.why: install.sh already creates and copies docs/specs/, the README makes a specific promise about what lives in git, and the memory plane's whole design argument is diffable prose. A second root forks the plane and hands librarian and drone-docs an ownership question nobody in the panel answered.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Unit-of-work noun (story vs ticket/task) and stage vocabulary language.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: "Story" everywhere; purge ticket and task. One user-facing word per stage, in English. Keep autopilot's rule, drop its word list.
conflict_resolutions.why: templates/story.md, worker-code.md, worker-test.md, docs/specs/ and scope-check.sh's own error text all say story, and the parser is keyed to a story file. Two nouns for one object is precisely the failure autopilot's rule was written against — the rule survives translation, the Russian vocabulary does not survive a public English MIT repo.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Spec mutability: autopilot amends the spec mid-build with a D## row; vulyk's plan is human-approved once and nothing contemplates editing it.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Allow it narrowly: a `## Plan deltas` section in plan.md, appended by the Queen only, one line per contradiction (what the plan assumed, what the code proved, at which story), written from the worker's RETURN REPORT and never from a diff, with a one-line notice to the human. Only invalidated stories are re-cut; landed stories stay landed. Not a route to drop a requirement, not a route for a good idea had while building.
conflict_resolutions.why: Without a path, the worker quietly builds something else and every downstream gate measures against a document that stopped being true — worse than an amended plan. Sourcing it from the return report rather than the diff keeps the Queen-never-reads-source rule intact, exactly as scout reports do; that has to be stated explicitly or the rule silently inverts into the Queen opening diffs.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Subagent continuation (дозапрос to the same worker, persistent reviewers).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Assume unavailable. Every repair is a fresh worker with the findings and the failing condition attached. Import only the two transferable rules: a hard ceiling of two repair rounds, and every repair stated as a checkable condition ("this test green"), never "improve it". Record in the constitution WHY the cheap path is unavailable so nobody re-derives it in six months.
conflict_resolutions.why: Native Task subagents are one-shot; continuation belongs to Agent Teams, which is experimental and env-gated and would break the README's no-experimental-flags promise. Autopilot's own phase file names fresh context as the correct fallback. Writing the недоделка/отказ cost distinction into vulyk-build.md before verifying resume-by-id would ship a rule the harness cannot honour.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Memory sourced from the plan vs from the code.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: drone-docs's primary source becomes the diff and the changed files; the story is passed only to name which files to look at and is explicitly labelled as a plan that may be wrong. If notes and diff disagree, the diff wins and the report says so. Add a verify-before-write checklist: every path named must exist, every command quoted must have been run, omit what cannot be verified.
conflict_resolutions.why: drone-docs.md says it receives "a diff or story file" and its step 1 tells it to read `## Implementation notes` first — so its own line 17 claim ("You record what IS, not what should be") is undercut by its input contract. A map slice describing an intention is worse than none, because CLAUDE.md:126 ("memory is a hint, verify against the code") assumes the hint was at least derived from code. drone-docs is a subagent, so handing it the diff costs the Queen nothing.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Who owns CLAUDE.md, and which marker convention wins.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: CLAUDE.md stays human- and /vulyk-evolve-owned. Generalise the existing marker pattern to exactly one more region: a VULYK:PROFILE pair around `## Project profile` that /vulyk-bootstrap and /vulyk-evolve write between, with install.sh's reset_commands_table() extended to blank it and reuse its existing loud-warning path. Code-derived architecture description goes to memory/map/ plus a new memory/overview.md, with CLAUDE.md carrying only a pointer.
conflict_resolutions.why: The VULYK:COMMANDS markers already exist and already have the right failure mode — warn loudly rather than silently ship the wrong thing, which is the 0.4.1→0.4.2 fix. Today /vulyk-bootstrap and /vulyk-evolve write into CLAUDE.md by prose instruction with no boundary at all, which on a brownfield repo with a team's hand-written constitution is an unbounded write. Real hole, worth closing; handing a subagent the whole file is not how to close it.

refuted.item: Persistent reviewer subagents / дозапрос (re-messaging a finished subagent with its context intact) — proposed across architecture, execution, quality and economy lenses; haiku/economy even invents a `persistAcrossTickets: true` frontmatter field.
refuted.reason: Not a native primitive. Task subagents are one-shot and no such frontmatter field exists. Resumption requires Agent Teams — experimental, env-gated (CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1), and it breaks vulyk's stated 'no experimental flags required' promise. Autopilot itself hedges it. Every cost argument built on it (amortised reviewer setup, cheap repair, cross-ticket panorama) collapses to 'always fresh context', which is what vulyk already does. Design for the fallback; stop quoting the savings.

refuted.item: state.js + dashboard.html as a mandatory v0.5.0 deliverable (haiku/architecture: 'mandatory — user-facing artifact justifying async design'; haiku/ux: ship it in the first slice).
refuted.reason: There is no async audience. The user is a solo operator sitting in the terminal that is producing the work. It is a 79KB HTML template plus a polled JS blob plus a write ritual threaded through every phase and every worker return — i.e. per-transition edits in the one context that is never refreshed — bought to render information the operator is already watching. It also duplicates story frontmatter `status:`, which /vulyk-status, the compact instructions and resume already read. Pure ceremony for this user.

refuted.item: haiku/execution: move story status out of frontmatter into a central state.js ('fragmented state', 'centralized is cleaner').
refuted.reason: Actively destructive. The frontmatter `status:` line is git-tracked, diffable, survives /clear, and is named explicitly in CLAUDE.md's compact-preservation list and read by /vulyk-status. Replacing it with an untracked JS blob for a single-operator setup loses resumability and creates two sources of truth during transition. The panel's own memory lens argues the opposite (git is truth) — this recommendation contradicts it.

refuted.item: The four-mode dial (full / semi / interview / manual), and specifically `full` mode — plus the parallel depth and polish dials.
refuted.reason: Three user-facing dials for one user who can simply say what they want in the prompt. `full` mode is a direct waiver of Law 1 and of the /vulyk-build approval marker — vulyk's only guard against an unattended agent spending an evening building the wrong thing on a real repo. The approval stop costs the operator thirty seconds. Autopilot needs modes because its user will not read a spec; this user will. The Tier matrix already routes ceremony, and adding a second authority over 'how much do I ask' guarantees the two disagree.

refuted.item: Autopilot's rule that tickets must not name file paths ('they go stale faster than the ticket'), conceding only directory-level zones.
refuted.reason: Would delete the framework's only deterministic, zero-token metric. `## Files` is parsed by scope-check.sh, is the Law 3 boundary, and — verified below — is also the only free way to detect that two parallel workers are about to write the same file. Autopilot's own zone rule concedes that path ownership has to be written down somewhere. vulyk wins outright; there is nothing to negotiate.

refuted.item: Rule 5 ('the orchestrator never writes the project's code, loses to no argument') adopted unconditionally.
refuted.reason: Head-on contradiction with Tier 0 ('do it directly, no ceremony') and with CLAUDE.md's delegation-restraint rule ('do not delegate what you can finish in a handful of tool calls'). Tier 0–1 is most of a solo user's traffic, and dispatching a fresh 20–40k-token worker context to change two lines is the exact overhead the rule claims to prevent. Only the scoped version is defensible — see conflict resolutions.

refuted.item: The full manifest apparatus: R##/R##.n/Ri/G##/A##/D## row taxonomy, seven statuses, five fixed update moments, and gates G1–G3 as mandatory artifacts (haiku/architecture and haiku/quality make this the v0.5.0 centrepiece).
refuted.reason: Requirement traceability is worth having; a ledger with a lifecycle is not. For this user the payload is one question — 'did it build what I asked?' — and that is answerable with a verbatim brief plus per-story requirement quotes plus a deterministic forward/backward trace script. The taxonomy adds bookkeeping in the one context that never refreshes, needs five synchronised update moments to stay honest, and G1 ('every row has a status') is bookkeeping over bookkeeping. Ship the value, refuse the ledger.

refuted.item: Three-axis review (Manifest/Spec/Craft) replacing lead-review's binary verdict, plus splitting review across two agents; haiku/quality also proposes replacing the ≤20-line-capped reviewer output.
refuted.reason: Two dispatches where one worked, a six-point protocol on one opus reviewer, and per-axis verdicts on a gate whose only consumer is a human deciding whether to merge. Splitting by axis buys no model diversity (unlike vulyk's Tier-4 different-model second reviewer, which is grounded in real precision/recall data). The transferable content is three named smells and one test-provenance question — four lines added to lead-review.md, not a reviewer roster.

refuted.item: memory/haiku: kill the SessionEnd learnings hook and replace it with phase-gated memory moments; drop /vulyk-gc consolidation from v0.5.0.
refuted.reason: Deletes the only cross-run learning mechanism in either framework in favour of one that fires only when the pipeline runs. For a solo user on long-lived repos, the framework getting measurably better at *their* codebase is the compounding value; a pipeline-only capture starves /vulyk-evolve's clustering threshold outright. Autopilot has no cross-run learning at all — this is importing an absence.

refuted.item: haiku/execution: raise the story token budget from ~1500 to ~2000 to match 'autopilot density'.
refuted.reason: An arbitrary number change with no evidence and no failure it fixes. The budget is a forcing function — the template says so explicitly — and it is orthogonal to the panel's separate (correct) argument that stories should be fewer and denser. Denser stories means fewer boundaries, not fatter files.

refuted.item: haiku/execution: drop `## Implementation notes` and `## Findings` free-form appends once the return contract lands; drop per-story drone-scout.
refuted.reason: Conflates the wire format with the on-disk record. The notes feed drone-docs and the memory plane after merge; the return block feeds the Queen during the build. Both are needed and they cost different things. Deleting the durable record to enforce brevity in the transient one is a straight loss.

refuted.item: The release-lens governance and positioning cluster: MAINTAINERS.md, security contact channel, bus-factor policy, README audience decision, npx skills.sh registration, bilingual README strategy, branding of the absorbed pipeline.
refuted.reason: None of these change what the framework does for the person running it. They are public-repo marketing and OSS-hygiene questions that have been smuggled into a merge decision. Real work, wrong forum, and they will consume the merge's editorial budget while the collision bug below stays unfixed.

refuted.item: Importing autopilot's 30-row Rationalizations table and 40-item Red Flags checklist into CLAUDE.md.
refuted.reason: ~9KB into a file loaded in every context including every subagent, defending machinery vulyk will not have (modes, доводка, waves bookkeeping, dashboard-vs-chat drift), in Russian, in an English repo. Worse, the Red Flags list is an instruction to the orchestrator to audit its own conduct — which CLAUDE.md explicitly forbids ('do not add instructions telling an agent to verify itself'). Roughly five rules survive; they fit in five lines.

refuted.item: Blind acceptance (G4) as an unconditional gate on every Tier 3-4 run.
refuted.reason: Presupposes a runnable product with a main scenario. A large share of this user's work is a library change, a migration, or a module refactor with nothing to walk — and vulyk's own `## Commands` table honestly ships 'Full suite / build: none exists' precisely because inventing a command that proves nothing is the bug v0.4.2 was released to fix. Unconditional G4 manufactures exactly that theatre. Keep it, make it conditional, and make 'I could not run this, here is why' an acceptable and loud outcome.

weak: Secrets/redaction, as framed. The gap is real (no secrets policy anywhere in CLAUDE.md — verified) but 'a live leak path today' is overstated: the default SessionEnd hook writes a stub, and the transcript path requires opting in with VULYK_AUTOLEARN=1 and asks Haiku for learnings, not raw text. Also note memory/learnings/ is committed *by design* (it ships a README and a real learnings file), so 'add it to .gitignore' would break the archive. The right fix is one redaction pass in the hook plus one line in the constitution — not a `## Secrets` section, a redact.sh, a Commands row, and a policy debate about hook fail-open semantics.

interfaces.md / a shared-contracts artifact, as a universal must. It earns its place only where a wave actually contains two or more concurrent stories — i.e. Tier 3-4. At Tier 2 (2–4 sequential-ish stories, the bulk of traffic) the map slice plus the story already covers it, and a third mandatory file per spec is drag. Ship it as a `## Contracts` section inside plan.md handed to workers in multi-story waves, not as a standalone file with its own lifecycle, writer discipline, and graduation rules into the memory plane.

The two-tier-scales conflict (vulyk Tier 0-4 vs autopilot T0-T3), which six lenses escalated to a headline decision. It is a rename, not a design question. One sentence settles it; the panel spent proportionally more words on it than on the silent-overwrite bug.

The `effort:` frontmatter contradiction, treated as a blocker on pipeline design. It blocks nothing: session-level effort is the shipping design and works. If the Aug-2026 docs turn out right, per-caste effort is pure upside added later. Worth one afternoon of measurement for the honesty of the README claim; not worth gating the merge on.

The 8-dimension depth pass (First run / Empty / Wrong input / Failure / Interruption / Growth / Boundaries / Aftermath) as a plan-time checklist. Genuinely useful as a prompt to the planner when writing acceptance criteria; genuinely bad as a mechanism that generates derived requirement rows. Take it as three lines in queen-planner.md, exempt from any story-count budget, and never as an artifact.

ADR harvest, D##-to-ADR routing, vocabulary ADRs, and the memory-moments restructure. All defensible for a team building institutional knowledge; near-zero return for one person who already remembers why they made the call and has /vulyk-evolve harvesting learnings. Keep lead-architect's existing ADR path; skip the harvest agent.

The 'Queen never runs the full verification suite in the main session' finding. Verified real (vulyk-build.md step 6) but its severity is inflated — it fires once, at the very end of a build, when the session is about to hand off to /vulyk-review anyway. Fix it because it costs one word, not because it is bleeding tokens all build.

Lazy per-phase file loading as a v0.5.0 item. Correct discipline, but vulyk's command bodies are 1–2KB and already load on invocation. It only becomes real if ~180KB of phase prose actually lands. State the rule in CONTRIBUTING.md; do not restructure anything yet.
top_musts: Refuse to co-dispatch two stories whose `## Files` blocks intersect, and compute waves (`wave = 1 + max(blockers)`, then split on file intersection) at plan time. VERIFIED BUG: vulyk-build.md step 2 says 'dispatch independent stories in parallel (cap: 4)' with no mechanism whatsoever to establish independence — story.md has no blocked_by and no zone, and nothing prevents two of the four concurrent workers from Editing the same file, where the loss is silent. The fix is nearly free because the machine-readable `## Files` block and an awk parser for it already exist in scope-check.sh. This is data loss, not a feature gap; it outranks everything else in the panel.

One commit per story, gated on scope-check + the story's green verification command, nothing committed on red. VERIFIED BUG: scope-check.sh defaults to working-tree-vs-HEAD and its own comment justifies this with 'VULYK's build loop does not commit per story' — so from story 02 onward, every scope check reports the *previous* stories' files as out of scope. The framework's only objective metric is contaminated by design after the first story of every multi-story build. Per-story commits fix it for free and add the rollback points the build loop currently has none of.

Launch a whole wave in a single message, one Task call per story. Two calls in two turns run serially and the transcript looks identical to a correct run — so today's 'cap: 4 concurrent' is plausibly a serial loop under a cap that never binds. One load-bearing sentence in vulyk-build.md step 3.

A bounded worker return contract: STATUS (DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT) / FILES / TESTS / INTERFACES / CONCERNS / BLOCKERS, ≤25 lines, no code and no diffs — plus a two-round repair ceiling (state the fix as a checkable condition; a third failure means the story was cut wrong, not implemented wrong). Today workers return whatever they like into the one context that is never refreshed. Keep `## Implementation notes` on disk as the durable record; the block is the wire format.

Write the human's request verbatim to `docs/specs/<slug>/brief.md` before any recon, never edited, later additions appended under a dated heading. One line of change in vulyk-plan.md. Today the earliest artifact vulyk produces is already a paraphrase, so nothing downstream can ever be compared against what was actually asked. Everything else worth taking from autopilot depends on this file existing.

Briefing question discipline in /vulyk-plan, Tier 2+: look facts up rather than asking (a fact about the repo is a drone-scout dispatch, never a question to the human); ask only what costs money, locks in a vendor, cannot be undone by editing, or encodes a business rule; one question at a time; every question carries a recommended default. Pure prompt text, no machinery, and it is the difference between a plan that matches intent and one that merely looks coherent. vulyk has no per-task clarification step at all today — ambiguity is only caught mid-build when a worker stops.

Conditional blind acceptance after PASS at Tier 3-4: a sonnet agent receives only brief.md, the repo, and the run command — never plan.md, never the story files — must actually run the thing and walk the main path, and reports per-criterion done/partial/missing with one line of evidence. If it cannot be run, it says exactly what blocked it and does not pass code-reading off as a run. Disagreement with the stories' status lines is reported as drift, never quietly reconciled. This is the only mechanism in either framework that can contradict the framework's own account of itself.

Story frontmatter gains `requirements:` (verbatim quotes from brief.md, ~40 tokens) plus a deterministic `scripts/trace-check.sh` running forward (every live requirement lands in ≥1 story) and backward (every story names ≥1 requirement). Zero tokens, no model, same shape as scope-check.sh, appends to memory/stats/. Backward is the direction vulyk has no defence against at all: an invented story burns a whole worker context and then confuses acceptance. This is the manifest's entire user value without the ledger.

Scope the Queen's hands to the build loop: from the moment a story file exists, the main session's keyboard reaches docs/specs/**, memory pointers and git add/commit/--stat — never a source file, never a diff, never the raw suite output (vulyk-build.md step 6 currently runs the full verification command in the main session). Explicitly refuse the two excuses that actually arrive: 'it's a two-line fix' and 'the worker failed, I'll finish it'. Tier 0–1 is exempt because there the Queen is the crew. This protects the one context in the design that is never refreshed, which is the actual failure mode of long solo sessions.

Irreversible or outward-facing actions are always a question, at any tier and any effort level: deploy, publish, pay, message a third party, delete data, rewrite git history. Stated in worker-code.md and worker-test.md, not only in CLAUDE.md — those are the two agents holding Bash with 40 and 30 turns, and a power user who has allowlisted Bash to cut permission prompts currently has no second line of defence anywhere in the framework.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Review timing: per-story review during the build (autopilot) vs a single adversarial gate at the end (vulyk). Flagged by architecture, execution, quality and economy lenses; three haiku analysts recommend switching the default.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Keep the single end-of-build lead-review gate as the only model review. Inside the build loop, the per-story check is deterministic only: scope-check.sh plus the story's own quiet verification command, both gating the commit. No lead-review dispatch per story at any tier.
conflict_resolutions.why: The amortisation autopilot relies on — a reviewer kept alive across tickets — is not available natively, so adopting per-story review buys the cost without the mitigation. Meanwhile a single reviewer reading the whole spec's diff catches 'story 05 contradicts story 02' by construction, for one dispatch. Per-story opus review is precisely the ceremony tax the 2026 landscape data punishes BMAD for.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Two complexity scales with the same name: vulyk Tier 0-4 (blast radius, decided before work) vs autopilot T0-T3 (product shape, decided at the cut).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: vulyk's Tier 0-4 is the only thing called a tier. Autopilot's scale is deleted; its story-count budgets and its >16 ceiling graft onto the existing rows of the routing matrix (Tier 0-1: none; Tier 2: 2-4; Tier 3: 4-8; Tier 4: 9-16; above 16 split into two specs).
conflict_resolutions.why: Tier is referenced by every command, every agent and the README, and it classifies before work starts — which is the routing decision that has to be made first. The counts are the transferable part; the vocabulary is pure collision.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Approval by default: /vulyk-plan stops unconditionally and /vulyk-build refuses without an approval marker, vs autopilot's default mode which shows the plan and starts, calling waiting 'the failure mode this skill exists to remove'.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: The gate stays unconditional. No mode may bypass it. Do not ship `full` mode at all; the tier matrix remains the only ceremony dial.
conflict_resolutions.why: Autopilot's default is right for a non-technical user dictating a greenfield app and wrong for an engineer operating on repos they own. The stop costs the operator thirty seconds and is the only thing standing between an unattended agent and an evening of wrong work on real code. Making it conditional is a change to safety behaviour dressed as an additive merge.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Rule 5 ('the orchestrator does not write the project's code') vs Tier 0 ('do it directly, no ceremony') and CLAUDE.md's delegation-restraint rule.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: The rule binds from the moment a story file exists — i.e. inside /vulyk-build, Tier 2 and up. Below that, the Queen is the crew and direct work is the correct protocol. State the boundary explicitly in the constitution rather than leaving both texts standing.
conflict_resolutions.why: Unscoped it contradicts the routing matrix in the same file and reads as decorative, which licenses violating it in either direction. Scoped, it protects exactly what it is for: the one context that survives to the end of a multi-story build.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Repair routing: same-context дозапрос with a 2× ceiling (autopilot) vs 'send a fresh worker with the findings attached' (vulyk-build.md step 4).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Fresh worker, always — but adopt the two transferable halves: state every repair as a checkable condition ('this test green', never 'improve it'), and cap it at two rounds before the story is marked blocked and handed back to planning. Do not design anything around subagent continuation or Agent Teams.
conflict_resolutions.why: Continuation is not a native primitive, so the cost distinction that motivates дозапрос does not exist here. The ceiling and the condition-phrasing survive the mechanism change intact and are the parts that actually prevent unbounded repair loops — which vulyk has no cap on today.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Spec mutability: autopilot's spec is amended in place whenever the build proves it wrong (D## row); vulyk's plan is human-approved once and executed, and vulyk-build.md step 4 lets the Queen 're-scope the story' unilaterally with no record.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Add a `## Plan deltas` section to plan.md: one Queen-written line per contradiction naming what the plan assumed and what the code proved, with a one-line notification to the human. Only the human may remove a requirement, quoted in their own words. The Queen may split or defer with a recorded `## Descoped` block on the story that surfaces at review — never silent narrowing.
conflict_resolutions.why: vulyk's current text authorises exactly the quiet requirement-narrowing that is the failure mode this whole merge exists to fix, and gives no path at all for 'the plan is wrong and the code proved it' — so plan.md quietly stops being true while every downstream gate keeps measuring against it. The delta line costs nothing and is the highest-value ADR source later.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Ceremony floor for the manifest: autopilot writes brief + manifest + spec for every run; vulyk Tier 0-1 explicitly refuses ceremony.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: brief.md and `requirements:` quotes turn on at Tier 2 and up; the trace-check runs whenever stories exist. Tier 0-1 gets none of it. Write this into the routing matrix as a rule, not a judgement call. The full row-ledger with seven statuses does not ship at any tier.
conflict_resolutions.why: A 25–50 row manifest for 'fix the retry in the uploader' — which is most of this user's traffic — is the exact ceremony-over-velocity failure that is currently killing heavyweight frameworks. Putting the floor in the matrix is what stops it drifting upward later.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Gate authority: autopilot's 'a failed gate is not a warning, the phase is redone' vs scope-check.sh's deliberate `exit 0` ('this reports, it does not block; blocking is lead-review's job').
conflict_resolutions.resolution: State it as policy in one line: deterministic scripts measure and never block; model verdicts can BLOCK; the human overrides either, out loud. All imported gates inherit vulyk's stance that the verdict is advice to the human, not authority over them.
conflict_resolutions.why: A deterministic check has deterministic false positives — an out-of-scope file is either a wide worker or a badly written story and the script cannot tell which. Auto-blocking on it trains planners to declare half the repo, which is the exact gaming the script's second number exists to catch. Model-judged gates are where blocking belongs.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Run-state visibility: dashboard/state.js as the source of truth vs vulyk's story frontmatter `status:` lines.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Frontmatter stays the source of truth. No dashboard. If resume proves painful, add a small run-state JSON derived from those status lines — read by /vulyk-status and named in the handoff dump — but never a second authority and never an HTML renderer.
conflict_resolutions.why: One operator, one terminal, no audience. The state file is the only half with a defensible job (surviving /clear, giving handoff a resume point); the renderer is a screenshot. Two sources of truth about 'where is the build' is how they drift apart.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: Model routing for the recon tier: CLAUDE.md says 'recon, docs, and memory upkeep on Haiku' while drone-scout.md, drone-docs.md and librarian.md all say `model: sonnet` (verified in the repo).
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Fix the doc to match the shipped files (sonnet) now, before any new cheap castes are assigned a model. Run the haiku-vs-sonnet scout comparison that docs/model-cascade.md already promises, then change both together if it favours haiku.
conflict_resolutions.why: The merge adds two or three more cheap castes; propagating an unresolved contradiction into new files multiplies it. And the constitution's model-routing claim is the framework's headline — a documented rule that the shipped agents contradict is the cheapest possible credibility loss.

conflict_resolutions.conflict: `effort:` in agent frontmatter: CLAUDE.md states it is silently ignored (measured July 2026); the current official subagent docs list it as supported. Raised as a blocker by architecture, economy and release lenses.
conflict_resolutions.resolution: Re-measure it (identical prompt, two agent files differing only in `effort:`, compare output tokens) and restate the claim with a date and client version, or retract it. Do not gate any pipeline design on the answer — ship session-level effort as-is.
conflict_resolutions.why: Session-level effort works today and is what the cascade is built on. If frontmatter effort turns out supported, per-caste effort is a pure addition later. The only thing genuinely at stake is a false statement in a constitution whose selling point is not overclaiming — that is a documentation fix, not a design blocker.
